checks.message: Creating an internet-facing load balancer
checks.context: Internet-facing load balancers are directly reachable from the public internet. This is expected for public-facing services. Ensure security groups restrict access to only required ports (80, 443) and that WAF is attached for application load balancers.

checks.message: Load balancer type not specified — defaults to 'application'
checks.context: The elbv2 API defaults to Application Load Balancer (ALB) when --type is omitted. Specify --type explicitly if you need a Network Load Balancer (NLB) for TCP/UDP or Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB). Classic Load Balancers use the separate 'elb' CLI namespace.

checks.message: Listener using unencrypted HTTP
checks.context: HTTP listeners transmit all traffic in plaintext. If this is a redirect listener (HTTP → HTTPS), this is expected and correct. Otherwise, create an HTTPS listener with a valid SSL certificate. Never terminate TLS at the load balancer with HTTP forwarding to backends over the public internet.

checks.message: Load balancer deletion will immediately drop all traffic
checks.context: Deleting a load balancer causes an immediate outage for all services behind it. Ensure DNS records are updated and traffic is drained before deletion.

checks.message: Verify SSL/TLS policy is not being downgraded
checks.context: Changing the SSL policy to an older version (e.g. ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08) enables weak ciphers and older TLS versions. Use ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06 or newer.

checks.message: Ensure API authentication and throttling are configured
checks.context: APIs without authentication are publicly accessible. Without throttling, a single client can overwhelm your backend. Configure API keys, Cognito authorizers, or IAM auth, and set usage plans with rate limits.

checks.message: Verify the stage has access logging and X-Ray tracing enabled
checks.context: Without access logging, you have no record of who called your API and with what parameters. Without X-Ray, you cannot trace requests through your backend. Both are critical for security monitoring.

checks.message: API deletion is permanent and immediately breaks all clients
checks.context: Deleting a REST API removes all resources, methods, stages, and deployments. All clients using this API will receive errors immediately. This action cannot be undone.

checks.message: Verify authentication is configured — HTTP APIs have no auth by default
checks.context: HTTP APIs (v2) are publicly accessible with no authentication unless you explicitly add a JWT authorizer or IAM auth. Unlike REST APIs, there's no API key support — use JWT authorizers with Cognito or a custom OIDC provider.

checks.message: Access logging not configured for this stage
checks.context: Without access logs you have no record of who called your API, what they sent, or what errors occurred. This is required for incident response and most compliance frameworks.

checks.message: HTTP API deletion immediately breaks all clients
checks.context: All routes, integrations, authorizers, and stages are destroyed. Any client using this API endpoint will fail immediately.

checks.message: Verify the default action is BLOCK, not ALLOW, for security-sensitive APIs
checks.context: A WAF ACL with a default ALLOW action only blocks traffic that matches your rules. For APIs handling sensitive data, consider a default BLOCK with explicit ALLOW rules for known-good traffic patterns.

checks.message: Deleting a WAF ACL removes all protection from associated resources
checks.context: Any CloudFront distribution, ALB, API Gateway, or AppSync API associated with this ACL immediately loses WAF protection. Disassociate the ACL from all resources before deleting.

checks.message: Verify the authorizer validates tokens correctly — misconfigured authorizers silently allow all requests
checks.context: A Lambda or Cognito authorizer that returns an allow policy without proper validation effectively makes the API public. Test with invalid tokens to confirm denials work.

checks.message: Store the client certificate private key securely — it authenticates your API Gateway to backends
checks.context: Client certificates enable mutual TLS between API Gateway and your backend. If the private key is exposed, anyone can impersonate API Gateway to your backend services.

checks.message: Changing subnets can cause brief connectivity disruption during reprovisioning
checks.context: The load balancer provisions new nodes in the new subnets and drains connections from old ones. If the new subnets lack proper route tables or NAT access, traffic will fail.

checks.message: Verify the web ACL rules are tested and won't block legitimate traffic
checks.context: Associating a WAF web ACL with a resource (ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway) immediately starts filtering traffic. Misconfigured rules can block legitimate users. Test in count mode before enforcing.

checks.message: Node-to-node encryption not enabled
checks.context: Without node-to-node encryption, data replication between cluster nodes is transmitted in plaintext. This is flagged by AWS Security Hub (OpenSearch.3). Enable it at domain creation — it cannot be added to an existing domain without creating a new one.

checks.message: Encryption at rest not enabled
checks.context: Without at-rest encryption, index data is stored unencrypted on disk. Encryption must be enabled at domain creation. Flagged by AWS Security Hub (OpenSearch.1).

checks.message: HTTPS not enforced on OpenSearch domain endpoint
checks.context: Without EnforceHTTPS=true, the domain accepts unencrypted HTTP connections, exposing search queries and results to interception. Flagged by AWS Security Hub (OpenSearch.8).

checks.message: OpenSearch domain not deployed in a VPC — domain may be publicly accessible
checks.context: Without VPC options, the domain is deployed with a public endpoint. Combined with a permissive access policy, this makes your search cluster accessible from the internet. Deploy in a VPC with private subnets.

checks.message: Domain deletion permanently destroys all indices and data — take a manual snapshot first
checks.context: There is no undo. All OpenSearch indices, dashboards, and configurations are permanently deleted. Take a manual snapshot to S3 before deleting if you need to retain any data.

checks.message: Verify you are not disabling encryption, HTTPS enforcement, or opening the access policy
checks.context: Domain config updates can disable security features. Disabling node-to-node encryption, at-rest encryption, or HTTPS enforcement exposes your search data. Verify the access policy is not being changed to allow public access (Principal: *).

checks.message: Verify the VPC endpoint security group restricts access to only trusted sources
checks.context: OpenSearch VPC endpoints provide private access to the domain from within a VPC. The security group attached to the endpoint controls which resources can connect. Ensure it restricts access to specific application security groups rather than broad CIDR ranges.

checks.message: Verify route tables are updated to route traffic through the firewall after creation
checks.context: Creating a Network Firewall does nothing until you update your VPC route tables to send traffic through the firewall endpoints. Traffic bypasses the firewall until routing is configured. Update route tables in both the firewall subnet and the protected subnets.

checks.message: Verify the default action is DROP or ALERT, not PASS, for stateless rules
checks.context: A firewall policy with a default stateless action of PASS allows all traffic that doesn't match a rule. For security-focused deployments, set the default action to DROP and explicitly allow only required traffic. Use ALERT to log traffic without blocking during initial deployment.

checks.message: Deleting the firewall immediately removes all traffic inspection — update route tables first
checks.context: Once the firewall is deleted, traffic that was routed through it will be dropped or bypass inspection depending on your route table configuration. Update route tables to bypass the firewall endpoints before deleting, or traffic will be black-holed.

checks.message: WAF ACL updates take effect immediately — verify rules don't block legitimate traffic
checks.context: Changes to a WAF web ACL are applied to all associated resources immediately. Adding overly broad rules can block legitimate users. Test new rules in count mode before switching to block mode, and monitor CloudWatch metrics for false positives.

checks.message: Verify the rule group is not referenced by any web ACL before deleting
checks.context: Deleting a rule group that is still referenced by a web ACL will fail. However, if you remove the reference first and then delete, the web ACL immediately loses those protection rules. Verify the impact on all associated resources before proceeding.

checks.message: Verify health check thresholds are appropriate for your application's response time
checks.context: Health checks with overly aggressive thresholds (short intervals, low failure thresholds) can trigger false failovers during brief latency spikes. Health checks with lenient thresholds delay detection of real outages. Tune the interval and failure threshold based on your application's normal response time.

checks.message: Verify no routing policies or CloudWatch alarms reference this health check
checks.context: Deleting a health check that is referenced by a Route 53 routing policy (failover, weighted, latency) removes the health evaluation for that record. The record may continue routing traffic to an unhealthy endpoint. Update routing policies before deleting.

checks.message: Verify the VPC is in a trusted account before associating with a private hosted zone
checks.context: Associating a VPC with a private hosted zone allows instances in that VPC to resolve the zone's DNS records. If the VPC belongs to an untrusted account, those instances gain access to your internal DNS namespace, potentially revealing internal service endpoints.

checks.message: Classic Load Balancers are deprecated — migrate to ALB or NLB
checks.context: Classic Load Balancers (ELB v1) are in maintenance mode and lack modern security features like SNI, HTTP/2, and advanced routing. AWS recommends migrating to Application Load Balancers (ALB) or Network Load Balancers (NLB). New deployments should use elbv2.

checks.message: Verify health check settings are appropriate for your application
checks.context: Target groups with lenient health check settings (high threshold, long interval) continue routing traffic to unhealthy targets for extended periods. Configure health checks with appropriate thresholds to detect failures quickly and remove unhealthy targets from rotation.

checks.message: Verify no listeners reference this target group before deleting
checks.context: Deleting a target group that is still referenced by a listener rule causes that rule to fail, dropping traffic for the affected routes. Remove all listener rules referencing this target group before deleting.

checks.message: Verify the certificate is valid and covers the correct domain names
checks.context: Adding an expired or domain-mismatched certificate to a listener causes TLS handshake failures for clients connecting to those domains. Verify the certificate's validity period and Subject Alternative Names before adding.

checks.message: Removing a certificate breaks HTTPS for all domains covered by that certificate
checks.context: Clients connecting to domains covered by the removed certificate will receive TLS errors. Verify no active traffic uses the domains covered by this certificate before removing it from the listener.

checks.message: Private CA creation is a significant security commitment — protect the CA key material
checks.context: A private Certificate Authority can issue certificates trusted by all systems in your organization. If the CA key is compromised, an attacker can issue certificates for any internal domain. Use a hardware security module (HSM) key storage and restrict CA administrator access to a small number of trusted principals.

checks.message: Deleting a CA revokes trust for all certificates it issued
checks.context: All certificates issued by this CA become untrusted once the CA is deleted. Any service using those certificates will experience TLS failures. Ensure all issued certificates are replaced before deleting the CA.

checks.message: Verify the certificate validity period is appropriate — avoid excessively long-lived certificates
checks.context: Certificates with multi-year validity periods increase the window of exposure if the private key is compromised. Use short-lived certificates (90 days or less) with automated renewal for internal services. Long validity periods are a compliance risk under most security frameworks.

checks.message: IAM signing certificates are legacy — use ACM or KMS for modern signing workflows
checks.context: IAM signing certificates are used for legacy SOAP-based AWS API authentication, which is no longer supported for most services. If you're using this for a modern workflow, consider whether ACM Private CA or KMS asymmetric keys are more appropriate.

checks.message: Direct Connect does not encrypt traffic in transit by default
checks.context: A dedicated circuit doesn't mean encrypted. Anyone with physical access at the colocation can intercept traffic. Use MACsec on dedicated connections or run an IPsec VPN over the DX connection for encryption.

checks.message: Deleting a Direct Connect connection immediately cuts all traffic using it
checks.context: If this connection carries production traffic, deletion causes an immediate outage. Verify failover to a backup DX connection or VPN is in place and tested before proceeding.

checks.message: Verify BGP peer IP, ASN, and VLAN with your network team before creating
checks.context: A wrong BGP config on a private VIF can black-hole traffic or advertise incorrect routes into your VPC. Mistakes here require a support ticket and colocation coordination to fix.

checks.message: Configure health checks on endpoint groups. Without them, traffic routes to unhealthy endpoints
checks.context: Global Accelerator doesn't know your endpoint is down unless you configure health checks. Set thresholds appropriate for your app's response time to avoid routing users to a broken backend.

checks.message: Disable the accelerator before deleting and update DNS records pointing to its static IPs first
checks.context: The two static Anycast IPs assigned to the accelerator are released on deletion. Any DNS records pointing to those IPs will route to released addresses that no longer serve your traffic. Update DNS before deletion.

checks.message: Disable auto-accept shared attachments unless you explicitly need it
checks.context: With auto-accept on, any account sharing an attachment to this TGW connects automatically. In a multi-account org this creates unintended network paths. Require explicit acceptance.

checks.message: Attaching a VPC to a TGW doesn't route traffic automatically. Update route tables
checks.context: You need to add routes in both the VPC route tables and the TGW route table. Also verify the attachment doesn't create unintended east-west connectivity between VPCs that should be isolated.

checks.message: Enable DNSSEC signing for public hosted zones
checks.context: Without DNSSEC, your domain is vulnerable to DNS spoofing and cache poisoning. Route 53 supports DNSSEC, so enable it for any public zone handling sensitive traffic.

checks.message: All DNS records are destroyed and services stop resolving immediately
checks.context: Export the zone file first. Update your domain registrar's nameservers if this zone was authoritative. Any service relying on these DNS names fails the moment the zone is deleted.

checks.message: DNS changes propagate globally within 60 seconds. Verify before submitting
checks.context: A wrong A record or CNAME redirects production traffic immediately. For critical records, lower the TTL to 60 seconds before making changes so you can revert quickly if something breaks.
